thread:
midfield_ops: Hey team — since ~08:26 UTC we're seeing p99 spikes on embeddings (tenant=midfield-prod). Baseline p99 ~600ms, now 3–6s for /v1/embeddings/bulk. Intermittent bursts every 10–30m. No API errors, just slow tails. Can you advise quick mitigations?

sam_support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste a sample request id or region? Also approx qps and average tokens per item? :eyes:

midfield_ops: region us-west-2, qps ~12 avg, some bulk calls ~64 items (each ~128 tokens). Sample request id: req_20260317_8a3f. No auth/billing errors.

devops-bot: ALERT: p99 latency > 2s for tenant=midfield-prod in us-west-2 on pool=gpu-pool-3. Runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/latency-tail-investigation :rotating_light:

priya_sre: tagging in — thanks for the sample. Early look at traces shows long GPU queueing and heavy KV cache misses for that route. Suspect noisy neighbor on that GPU pool (large bulk embeds). Two quick options: 1) apply per-tenant soft throttle to limit concurrent requests OR 2) move midfield-prod to a priority lane / reserved slice while we investigate.

alyssa_cs: For customer impact — midfield has a paid reserved tier. We can request a temporary bespoke allowlist so their routes bypass general throttles until we finish root cause. Need signoff from product to change routing.

sam_support: Priya — can you apply a short-term throttle we can roll back? Maybe cap concurrent bulk requests to 3 or rps to 8? That should reduce queuing. I'll tell the customer to reduce batch size as well.

priya_sre: Doing throttle: applying per-tenant token-bucket on /v1/embeddings/bulk for midfield-prod -> limit 8 rps, burst 2. Will monitor.

michael_prod: If we do priority lane, ops will need a CIDR and list of routes to allow. Also note priority lane reduces cost efficiency for that pool. Recommend throttle first, then allowlist if customer SLA requires it.

midfield_ops: Throttle sounds fine short-term. We can also reduce batch size on our side to 16 items. Will coordinate deploy in ~5min. Thanks.

sam_support: FYI reproducer steps for eng: `curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings/bulk" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"tenant":"midfield-prod","items":[...64 items...]}'` — reproduces p99 locally against us-west-2 pool.

priya_sre: Noted. Also one-off tip: set `max_concurrency` header or `max_tokens_per_batch` to avoid huge KV churn. Example quick patch to client:```js
// reduce batch size client-side
client.embedBulk(items.slice(0,16))
```

devops-bot: ACTION: throttle applied to tenant=midfield-prod on route=/v1/embeddings/bulk at 09:02:12 UTC. Monitor link: https://internal.redwood/mon/alerts/2367899999

sam_support: I told the customer we applied a short throttle and asked them to reduce batches. They acknowledged. :white_check_mark:

priya_sre: Early telemetry after throttle: p99 dropped from ~3.2s to ~920ms within 3 minutes. p95 stable near 450ms. We'll keep the throttle for 1 hour while we trace noisy actor.

alyssa_cs: I'll open a reservation/allowlist ticket with midprod business owner for priority lane evaluation. If they sign, we can add bespoke allowlist to skip soft throttles and schedule migration to a reserved pool.

midfield_ops: Thanks everyone. Please keep us posted. We'll also roll a client patch to cap batches to 16 in the next deploy.

priya_sre: Follow-ups: collect flame graphs for GPU pool, list top tenants by token-seconds, and check kernel scheduling; I'll take ownership and post updates here. Closing note: mitigation applied and effective — leaving open while root cause work continues.
